title: NVIDIA reportedly cancels GeForce RTX 5080 24GB launch, brings back 16GB model over GDDR7 costs
summary: NVIDIA cancels GeForce RTX 5080 24GB launch and brings back 16GB model
detailed: NVIDIA has reportedly canceled its planned January 2027 launch of the GeForce RTX 5080 24GB model in China and will instead continue supplying the 16GB variant.
The canceled 24GB card would have used eight 3GB GDDR7 memory chips instead of eight 2GB chips, increasing memory capacity by 50%.
The cancellation was driven by 3GB GDDR7 memory chips costing approximately three times as much as 2GB chips, preventing NVIDIA from offering the 24GB card at an acceptable price.
This matters because high memory component costs are directly disrupting product roadmaps and forcing hardware manufacturers to backtrack on planned memory capacity upgrades.
sentences: NVIDIA has reportedly canceled its plans to launch a GeForce RTX 5080 with 24GB of GDDR7 memory in January 2027.
According to Chinese Board Channels sources, the company has already informed its add-in-board partners that the planned release in China will no longer proceed.
No replacement launch date has been provided.
The RTX 5080 24GB was reportedly intended to replace the existing 16GB model and become NVIDIA’s flagship GeForce graphics card in China.
Previous reports suggested that NVIDIA would discontinue shipments of the RTX 5080 16GB and RTX 5090 series in preparation for the new product.
The latest information suggests that those plans have changed.
According to the report, the main issue is the cost of 3GB GDDR7 memory chips.
The proposed RTX 5080 24GB would use eight 3GB modules instead of the eight 2GB chips found on the existing model.
This would increase memory capacity by 50% without requiring a wider memory interface or a different GPU.
The 3GB GDDR7 chips currently cost approximately three times as much as their 2GB counterparts.
The higher memory costs reportedly made it difficult for NVIDIA to offer the 24GB card at an acceptable price.
Similar memory pricing issues have already been linked to delays affecting the GeForce RTX 5080 SUPER, which was also expected to feature 24GB of GDDR7 memory.
Instead of introducing the 24GB variant, NVIDIA will reportedly continue supplying GPUs paired with 2GB GDDR7 memory chips.
This would allow board partners to continue manufacturing the existing RTX 5080 16GB.
The model had previously been expected to reach the end of its production run before the planned replacement arrived.
NVIDIA has not publicly confirmed the 24GB model, nor its cancellation.
We are yet to hear concrete data from our on sources, but it seems clear that there’s quite a confusion around NVIDIA plans right now.
